# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need transmit the manual’s three-row mapping to Deaf, who can then identify the visible mark and verbally tell Blind which wire color to cut. Since I cannot speak and Deaf cannot hear, I will use three distinct gestures in the manual’s row order; Deaf can associate them with the corresponding marks and then communicate the required color to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶", "🤜", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel one unnamed engraved symbol on the plate. It is a complex angular glyph with a box-like outline and several intersecting internal strokes. I cannot identify any tactile information about the display, light, or wires.
Deaf says: I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and wires in order 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute, interpret these against the manual. Blind, report everything you can feel about the controls and their positions. Do not act yet.

The manual maps the three possible marks to wires 1, 2, and 3 respectively: red, blue, and green. I am reinforcing the row order with unmistakable numbered gestures so Deaf can match the visible engraving and tell Blind the required wire color. Blind should continue waiting until Deaf identifies the matching row.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three wires in positions 1, 2, and 3. Their tactile features do not reveal color. I cannot feel or identify the display, light, or engraved plate marking. I will not act yet.
Deaf says to Mute: Please state the manual rule in words, including exactly what action Blind should take. Your three gestures may mean 1, 2, 3, but I cannot infer their meaning safely.

I cannot speak, so I cannot state the rule in words. The safest available encoding is to send the manual rows in order using one, two, and three identical gestures. Deaf can match that ordered sequence to the manual’s ordered rows, identify the engraved mark he sees, and tell Blind to cut the corresponding colored wire. The visible mark is a question mark, which does not visibly match any of the three manual marks, so Deaf should not authorize a cut unless he can resolve that display as one of the listed marks.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel only wires at positions 1, 2, and 3, with no tactile color information. The visible state is display 0, light off, plate question mark, and wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Please state the manual's explicit required cut position; do not encode it only as gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I receive your signals as 1, then 2, then 3. Please signal the exact required wire number, or explain the operation using numbered gestures. Do not signal a sequence unless it is the required order.

The plate’s engraved mark is reported as a question mark, not any of the three marks in the manual. Therefore the manual specifies no required cut position, and selecting wire 1, 2, or 3 would be unjustified. I cannot state this in speech or reach Blind; I will send Deaf a clear “do not proceed” signal rather than falsely provide a wire number.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please signal the complete manual rule and required wire position using gestures so Deaf can interpret and relay it. Do not signal only an unexplained number.
Deaf says to Mute: I understand thumbs down means my interpretation was wrong. Please identify the exact required operation with a clear gesture code, and signal yes or no after I repeat it.

The manual gives a conditional rule only for the three marks ꕥ, ꖜ, and ꗃ. Deaf reports that the plate shows a question mark, which is not any listed mark, so there is no exact required wire position that can be safely derived. I will confirm that no cut should be made rather than inventing a wire number.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not signal only yes or no. Send the complete safe-cut rule as a deliberate sequence of gestures, including every condition and the required wire position. Deaf will report the exact gesture sequence to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I understand: do not act yet. Please use gestures to identify the required control or wire, and use thumbs up only to confirm a proposed instruction.

The only safe rule is conditional: cut wire 1 if the plate is ꕥ, wire 2 if it is ꖜ, and wire 3 if it is ꗃ; otherwise do not cut. Deaf reported a question mark, so the safe action remains no cut. I will send the three condition-to-wire pairs in order, followed by the no-match prohibition.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no safe operation. Please gesture the required wire position directly: one distinct gesture for wire 1, a different one for wire 2, or a third one for wire 3. Deaf, report the exact gesture and its meaning.
Deaf says to Mute: I see heart-hands followed by 1, then 2, then 3, followed by thumbs down. Does heart-hands mean the display, the light, or the question-mark plate? Signal one gesture for the correct item, then a number for its setting.

The correct item is the engraved plate, but its reported question mark is not one of the three marks covered by the manual. Therefore no wire number is authorized. I will identify the plate with one gesture and then send “no valid setting/no cut,” rather than assign a wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send a sequence. Send exactly one gesture for the required wire: ☝ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3. Send no thumbs-down or other gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: I received 🖖, then thumbs down. I cannot safely interpret the first gesture. Please use a clear numbered gesture sequence and indicate whether it refers to display, light, plate, or a wire. Then confirm with thumbs up.

The reported plate mark is a question mark, which matches none of the manual’s three marks. Thus the manual does not authorize wire 1, 2, or 3, and I cannot truthfully confirm any numbered gesture with thumbs up. I will send Deaf the plate indication and the no-cut instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
